name: Absalom
description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy

points: Sons were born to David in Hebron: the firstborn Amnon of Ahinoam, Chileab of Abigail, Absalom the son of Maachah the daughter of the king of Geshur, Adonijah the son of Haggith, Shephatiah of Abital, and Ithream of Eglah his wife.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Absalom, her older brother, told her not to worry about it for now. But Absalom was one of those men who holds a grudge for years just to get someone back for it, and remember these are people who know the law and know they are Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: When King David heard all these things he was very wroth. And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had forced his sister Tamar.
David was upset at what happened to Tamar but did not do anything about it. Absalom said nothing to Amnon, but he was quietly holding on to the offense, waiting.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: After two full years Absalom had sheepshearers in Baalhazor beside Ephraim and invited all the king's sons. He pressed David to come, and when David would not, he pressed that Amnon and all the king's sons go with him, and the king let them go.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom was setting Amnon up. He specifically maneuvered to get Amnon out of the city and among his own servants.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom told them to wait until Amnon was drunk and merry with wine, then to strike, and killed him for what he did to Tamar.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom commanded his servants to mark when Amnon's heart was merry with wine, and when he gave the word to smite and kill him, to fear not, for he had commanded them. The servants did as Absalom commanded, and all the king's sons arose, every man got upon his mule, and fled.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: While they were on the way, tidings came to David that Absalom had slain all the king's sons and not one was left. The king arose, tare his garments, and lay on the earth. But Jonadab said not to suppose all were slain, for Amnon only was dead; by the appointment of Absalom this had been determined from the day Amnon forced his sister Tamar.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom fled, and the watchman saw much people coming, and Jonadab confirmed the king's sons had come as he said. The king's sons came, lifted up their voice and wept, and the king and all his servants wept very sore. Absalom fled to Talmai the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, and David mourned for his son every day, and was there three years; and the soul of David longed to go forth to Absalom, being comforted concerning Amnon since he was dead.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: The king told Joab he had done this thing, and commanded him to go bring the young man Absalom again. Joab fell on his face, thanked the king, and said he now knew he had found grace in the king's sight. Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem, but the king said, Let him turn to his own house and not see my face.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: Joab set the whole thing up to get Absalom back. David showed mercy by letting him return to Jerusalem, but said, Tell him not even to come see me; go to his own house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: Absalom was trying to get the king's attention, and when Joab would not respond, he set the man's field on fire to force the matter. This was straight craziness, but it finally brought him before the king, and David kissed him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem and saw not the king's face. He sent for Joab twice to send him to the king, but Joab would not come, so Absalom had his servants set Joab's barley field on fire. Then Joab came, and Absalom said, Let me see the king's face, and if there be any iniquity in me, let him kill me. Joab told the king, and Absalom came and bowed himself, and the king kissed Absalom.

note.label: 2 Samuel 14: Joab Brings Absalom Home

points: Absalom prepared chariots and horses and fifty men to run before him, rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate. When any man came to the king for judgment, Absalom called him, said his matters were good and right but there was no man deputed of the king to hear him, and wished that he himself were made judge in the land that he might do every man justice.

This is the sneakiness Absalom did: he began to underhand the king, winning the love of the people behind the king's back, so that he could later betray him, as the prophecy said the sword would not depart from David's house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 15: Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel

points: When any man came near to do him obeisance, Absalom put forth his hand, took him, and kissed him, and on this manner he did to all Israel that came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

Instead of going to the king and resolving things, Absalom got into the king's good graces, then went around patting people on the back and stroking them. This is what the bishop calls friendish, showing people friendship without being a true friend.

note.label: 2 Samuel 15: Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel

points: After forty years Absalom asked leave to go pay his vow in Hebron, and the king said, Go in peace. But Absalom sent spies through all the tribes to say, at the sound of the trumpet, Absalom reigneth in Hebron. Two hundred men went with him from Jerusalem in their simplicity, knowing nothing. Absalom also sent for Ahithophel, David's counsellor, and the conspiracy was strong, for the people increased continually with Absalom.

note.label: 2 Samuel 15: Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel

points: David, being the man of war that he is, saw everyone starting to follow Absalom, and instead of sitting there like a dummy, chose to leave and strategize while he was out.

note.label: 2 Samuel 15: Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel

points: A messenger told David the hearts of the men of Israel were with Absalom, and David told his servants to arise and flee, lest Absalom overtake them suddenly and smite the city with the sword. The king went forth with all his household, leaving ten women who were concubines to keep the house, and all his servants and the Cherethites, Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites passed on before him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 15: Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel

points: Ahithophel was such a good counsellor that his counsel was said to be like inquiring at the oracle of God, like talking to an angel of the Most High. So David prayed the Most High would turn that counsel into foolishness, and sent his friend Hushai to act like Absalom's servant so he could listen to Ahithophel's counsel and intervene. This was a game of chess, not checkers, and that is how we have to treat this thing today.

note.label: 2 Samuel 15: Absalom Steals the Hearts of Israel

points: The Lord hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the Lord hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son. So here it is. This brother from the house of Saul, meaning from the tribe of Benjamin, is now showing his hatred or disdain for King David for the kingdom being translated over to him. He is blaming King David for Saul's death. He is blaming King David for everything. And in that anger he begins to cast stones at David and his mighty men. Now he is saying, the fact that Absalom is hunting for you, you deserve it, because of all the bloodiness that you did. Now Absalom is doing it to you.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: As David came to Bahurim, a man of the house of Saul named Shimei the son of Gera came out, cursing and casting stones at David and all his servants. Shimei cursed, calling David a bloody man and a man of Belial, saying the Most High had returned upon him all the blood of the house of Saul, and delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom his son, and taken him in his mischief because he was a bloody man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: David and his men went by the way while Shimei went along the hillside cursing, throwing stones, and casting dust; and they came weary and refreshed themselves. Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him. When Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom saying, God save the king, Absalom asked why he went not with his friend, and Hushai answered that he would serve whom the Most High and Israel chose, and would serve in the presence of the son as he served the father.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: Hushai put into action the plan he and David made. Absalom challenged him, asking, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? Why wentest thou not with thy friend? This is a real friend, not a friendish one; a true friend tells you when you are wrong and full of it, not the one who only strokes your head and pats your back like Absalom did to steal the people's hearts.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: Absalom asked Ahithophel for counsel, and Ahithophel said, Go in unto thy father's concubines whom he left to keep the house, and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father, and the hands of all with thee shall be strong. So they spread Absalom a tent on the top of the house, and Absalom went in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel. The counsel of Ahithophel was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God.

Ahithophel counselled Absalom to lie with the ten concubines David left, in the sight of all Israel, on the roof of the house. This is the exact fulfillment of what the Most High spoke in chapter 12, that David's wives would be taken and one would lie with them in the sight of the sun, and that what David did secretly would be done before all Israel. It was not coincidence or irony; it was prophesied to happen, and none of it would have happened if David had not done what he did. The Most High keeps mercy and forgives, but by no means clears the guilty, so even when we come in and repent, we still must remember the fear of the Most High, for there is but one step between us and death.

note.label: 2 Samuel 16: Ziba, Shimei's Cursing, and Absalom Defiles the Concubines

points: Ahithophel had already given Absalom wicked counsel in the previous chapter, telling him to go in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel so that the hands of all that were with him would be made strong. Ahithophel was David's own counselor turned traitor, being the devil the Bible speaks of, working deceit and betrayal from inside the gates of Israel.

Now he asks Absalom to let him choose out twelve thousand men to pursue David that same night while David was weary and weak handed, to smite the king only and bring back all the people. He wanted the victory and the bragging rights of being the one who killed King David.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

points: Absalom wanted a second opinion, so he called Hushai the Archite to hear likewise what he would say. There is safety in a multitude of counselors, but only where the counsel is according to thus saith the Lord; a counselor who does not go to the scriptures is not one you should want.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

points: Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

points: The messengers Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited by En-rogel; a maidservant carried the word to them, but a lad saw them and told Absalom. The Most High put His spirit on certain people to orchestrate His plan; often when a man tries to do evil to another, it falls back on him, for he that diggeth a pit shall fall therein.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

points: They fled to a man's house in Bahurim that had a well, and a woman spread a covering over the well's mouth and ground corn upon it to camouflage it. When Absalom's servants came asking, she told them the men had gone over the brook of water, and the pursuers returned to Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

points: David charged Joab, Abishai, and Ittai to deal gently for his sake with the young man, even with Absalom, and all the people heard the charge. Even after Absalom defiled his concubines and stole the people's hearts, David still sought to make amends with his son.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: Absalom, riding on a mule, went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak so that he was taken up between the heaven and the earth while the mule went on. He hung there yet alive.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: A man told Joab he had seen Absalom hanged in an oak. Joab asked why he had not smitten him to the ground for a reward of ten shekels and a girdle, but the man refused, saying he would not put forth his hand against the king's son for a thousand shekels, because he had heard the king charge them to beware that none touch the young man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: The man told Joab that to have killed Absalom would have been to work falsehood against his own life, for nothing is hid from the king, and Joab himself would have set himself against him. Joab said he would not tarry, took three darts, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: Joab was an evil man with the spirit of murder; he could have brought Absalom back alive for his father to make amends, but he did what he wanted. Ten young men that bore Joab's armor compassed Absalom and smote him and slew him, for a beast will consort to his own like.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: Joab blew the trumpet and held back the people from pursuing Israel. They took Absalom, cast him into a great pit in the woods, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him, and all Israel fled everyone to his tent.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: In his lifetime Absalom had reared up a pillar for himself in the king's dale, saying he had no son to keep his name in remembrance, and he called it after his own name; it is called Absalom's place unto this day.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: Cushi came and said the enemies of the king and all that rose against him should be as that young man is. David understood that his son was one of the casualties of war. He was much moved, went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept, crying, O my son Absalom, would God I had died for thee. David's whole life was war, slaughtering giants from his youth up, and now he mourned in heartache for his son.

note.label: 2 Samuel 18: Deal Gently With the Young Man

points: All the tribes of Israel were at strife, saying the king had saved them from the Philistines and their enemies but had fled the land because of Absalom, who was now dead, so why did they say nothing about bringing the king back.

note.label: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

points: Rehoboam takes Mahalath and Abihail as wives who bear him children, then takes Maachah the daughter of Absalom, whom he loves above all his wives and concubines.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: Read this psalm remembering the heading: it is a psalm of David when he fled from Absalom his son. If you do not know that history, go back to Second Samuel and read it. Try to put yourself in the scriptures to better your understanding, because things written the fourth time were written for our learning, that through the patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

note.label: Psalm 3: But Thou O Lord Art a Shield for Me
